statusHelp.historically_documented: Established by primary records such as official documents, court records or contemporaneous evidence.
statusHelp.supported_by_evidence: Backed by credible evidence, but not fully established.
statusHelp.partially_supported: Some elements are supported, others are not.
statusHelp.disputed: Credible sources disagree; the evidence is contested.
statusHelp.unverified: Claimed, but not supported by verifiable evidence.
statusHelp.under_investigation: Currently being reviewed by the editors.

home.lead: Explore theories, mysteries and documented secret operations on a giant investigation wall. Every claim is linked to its sources.
home.p1Text: Each entry lists its central claims individually, each with its own sources. Editorial ratings are kept separately under Expert opinions.
home.p2Text: Sources are linked to the specific claim they support or refute, never to a whole article by default.
home.p3Text: Anyone can submit a theory, with a display name or anonymously. Every submission is reviewed first.
home.sticky: Follow the sources, not the noise.

wall.title: Investigation Wall
wall.intro: Drag to move, scroll to zoom, double-click a card to focus. Red threads show how entries are connected.
wall.localNote: Views and your own card arrangement are stored only in this browser.
wall.connectHint: Select two cards (click, then Shift+click) to draw a thread.
wall.stressTest: Synthetic performance test data ({count} cards) – not saved.
wall.autoThreads: Automatic threads (same person, organization or place)
wall.autoThreadNote: Detected automatically from the archive. A shared name alone is not evidence that the cases are connected.

archive.title: Theory Archive
archive.intro: Every case file separates historical facts from further claims and links each claim to its sources.
archive.communityHint: Theories from the community are mixed into the archive and carry this stamp.

theory.claimHint: The central claims of this entry, each with the sources attached to it. A source only counts for the claim it is attached to.
theory.noEvidence: No source attached to this claim.
theory.communityNote: Community contribution. The editors have not yet verified its claims.

orgs.title: Organizations
orgs.intro: Agencies, institutions, commissions and groups that appear in the archive.

events.title: Historical Events
events.intro: Dated events referenced by the archive, from the 18th century to today.

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.intro: Events above the red thread, case files below it. Zoom from centuries to single years, drag to travel through time and select an entry to see what it is connected to.
timeline.selectEvent: Select an event or a case file on the tape. Its connections are drawn in red.

timeline.keys: Arrow keys move, plus and minus zoom, Escape clears the selection.
timeline.yearWikidata: Year as stated on the case's Wikidata item.
timeline.yearEvents: Span of the events this case file is linked to.

map.title: World Map
map.intro: Case files, historical events and organizations, pinned where the archive names a place. The map data is bundled locally; no external map service is used.
map.selectPlace: Select a place on the map.
map.casesPlaced: {placed} of {total} case files have a place

investigations.title: Investigations
investigations.intro: Your private research projects: notes, hypotheses, sources, counter-arguments, document links, a private board and a timeline.
investigations.privacy: Private by default. Your projects are linked to a secret key stored in this browser. Nothing becomes public unless you submit it for review yourself.
investigations.keyHelp: Keep a copy of this key to open your investigations on another device. Anyone with the key can read and edit them.
investigations.keyInvalid: A key consists of 64 hexadecimal characters.
investigations.publishHint: Opens the editor pre-filled with this investigation. It is only published after moderation.
investigations.threadsSuggested: Threads on your private board are always marked as suggested.

community.title: Community conspiracy theories
community.intro: Conspiracy theories submitted by visitors from around the world. Every entry has passed moderation before it is published.
community.anonymity: Contributors can publish under a display name or as "Anonymous".
community.empty: No community contributions have been published yet.
community.step1: You submit your text with sources.
community.step3: Approved contributions are published, marked as community content and initially rated "Unverified".
community.step4: Published entries appear on the Investigation Wall with suggested connections.
community.disclaimer: These theories come from the community. Many of them cannot be verified easily, so the editors have not checked their claims. Read them critically and look at the sources.
community.badgeHelp: Submitted by the community – claims not verified by the editors

submit.subtitle: Subtitle (optional)

submit.privacy: We store only what you enter here. No account, no e-mail address.

knowledge.title: Knowledge Archive
knowledge.intro: Documents, sources and the methodology behind the archive.
knowledge.primaryText: Primary sources are original records from the time or from the actors involved: memoranda, court records, hearing transcripts, official reports, data. Secondary sources analyse or report on them: books, articles, reference works.
knowledge.qualityText: Each source carries a note explaining what it can and cannot show. An original publication of a theory is a primary source for the history of that theory, not evidence that the theory is true.
knowledge.linkingText: A source is attached to the specific claim or counter-argument it supports or refutes. A source never counts as proof of every claim in an entry.
knowledge.expertsLink: Evidence ratings and their scale are listed under Expert opinions

about.title: About
about.text1: The Conspiracy Atlas is an international archive that documents conspiracy theories, historical mysteries, documented secret operations and the connections between them.
about.text2: It does not promote any theory. The archive presents the content neutrally and links every statement to its sources. Editorial assessments of the evidence are collected separately under Expert opinions.
about.costText: The site runs exclusively on free plans of Cloudflare Pages, Workers, D1 and Turnstile. Images are compressed in the browser and stored in the free D1 database under a hard storage cap; paid storage services are not used. Features that would require paid or usage-billed services stay disabled and are marked "Currently unavailable!". When a free limit is reached, the affected feature pauses until the limit resets or space is freed.
about.privacyText: No user accounts, no tracking, no advertising, no external fonts or scripts (except Cloudflare Turnstile on submission forms when enabled). Contributions store only the display name you choose. IP addresses are never stored in readable form; anti-abuse counters use salted hashes and are deleted within a day.
about.licensesText: All illustrations are original works created for this project. Fonts and libraries are used under their open-source licenses (see LICENSES.md in the repository). Linked documents remain with their publishers.

images.hint: Images are compressed in your browser and published with this case file right away. Only use images you are allowed to publish and name the source under "Image credit".

admin.notesIntro: Sources and comments that visitors added to case files. Approved notes appear on the case page.

users.imagesIntro: Profile images are public at once. Delete anything illegal here; locking an account also hides its images.

users.confirmAdmin: Give @{name} admin rights? The account can then open the admin area with its normal login.

search.label: Search the archive
search.hint: Type at least 2 characters. Tip: press Ctrl K or / anywhere.

experts.title: Expert opinions
experts.intro: The archive itself is neutral and only presents the content. This section collects the editors’ assessments of how well each case and each claim is supported by the evidence.
experts.caseNote: These ratings are an editorial assessment of the available evidence. The archive entry itself presents the case without a rating.

saved.title: Saved cases & my wall
saved.intro: Bookmark case files and arrange them on your own wall. Everything is stored only in this browser, without an account; nothing is sent to the server.
saved.empty: You have not saved any case files yet. Open a case file and click "Save".
saved.wallHint: Drag cards, select two cards to tie a thread, add your own notes under "Filters". Click "Save layout in this browser" to keep the arrangement. Dotted threads are found automatically (same person, organization or place).

notes.title: Notes from readers
notes.intro: Additional sources and comments from visitors. They are published only after an editor has approved them; approval does not mean the content has been verified.
notes.moderationHint: Your note is checked by an editor before it appears. Only the display name is stored, no e-mail or IP address.
notes.sent: Thank you! Your note will appear after an editor approves it.

login.title: Sign in
login.intro: Sign in to design your own profile page and collect your case files.

register.title: Create an account
register.intro: An account gives you your own profile page that you can design yourself.
register.privacy: No e-mail address needed. We store your username, a hash of your password and what you put on your profile, nothing else.

recover.title: Reset your password
recover.intro: Enter your username and the recovery code you received when you signed up.

fields.usernameHelp: 3–24 characters: a–z, 0–9, "-" and "_". Your profile address will be /u/username.

errors.mismatch: The two passwords are not the same.
errors.recovery: Username or recovery code is wrong.
errors.locked: This account has been locked by the editors.

recovery.title: Your recovery code
recovery.text: Keep this code somewhere safe. It is the only way to reset your password, because we do not store an e-mail address. It is shown only once.

empty.about: Write a few lines about yourself in the editor.
empty.favorites: Pick favourite case files from your saved cases.

empty.links: Add links to your website or social media.
